entry.content:
Author: bbayles
Posted: Tue Nov 17, 2026 2:28 am (GMT 0)

The Yu Yu Hakusho Spirit Skannerz discussion reminded of me about a family Christmas gathering.

One of my uncles had recently got married and brought a stepson to Christmas. The stepson was not happy about having to spend the holiday with strangers, and was mopey and sullen the whole time. Several relatives had gotten him Christmas gifts as a welcome to the family, but he wasn't having any of it. He sat in the corner and played with his Skannerz toy.

I realized that they worked with any barcode, so I went to the computer and printed off several dozen sheets of random barcodes. This totally won him over, and Christmas was saved!

Alas, his wasn't the Yu Yu Hakusho Spirit Skanner.

entry.title: Development :: RE: Long lost cheat codes
entry.dc:creator: bbayles
entry.dc:subject: Development
entry.content:
Author: bbayles
Posted: Mon Nov 16, 2026 11:53 pm (GMT 0)

Next up was Taz-Mania for Game Gear!

  • Pause during gameplay
  • While holding 1, press Left, Left, Right, Right.
  • While holding 2, press Right, Right, Left, Left.
  • Press Start


A cheat menu appears! It lets you choose which level to play.

I actually got to talk to Mac Senour, Sega's producer for this game for the Hidden Palace podcast. The interview is up on YouTube (@HiddenPalace) and on podcast indexes. He talks a lot about Taz-Mania and other Game Gear games he worked on.

entry.dc:creator: mateusbond
entry.dc:subject: Website
entry.content:
Author: mateusbond
Posted: Mon Nov 16, 2026 11:08 pm (GMT 0)

Well guys, I think I'll be slowing down for the moment. I have a newborn second child (first daughter!), she takes most of my free time, and while I would love to spend the free time of my free time playing SMS homebrew, the truth is they're all AI ports nowadays, thanks to this current AI craze, and they're all ports of games that play better, look better, control better and are less bug prone on their original systems, which means I have little to zero interest in spending half an hour of my day playing them to take screenshots, and another half hour to gather info and edit a readme, that most of the times (surprise!) is also written by an AI. But oh, no, I'm not giving up. It's just a warning that updating the Homebrew section on a daily basis, like I've been doing for some time now, may become unsustainable for a while. The list this thread started with will probably return, and I'll certainly be faster than Sonic when it comes to adding No AI stuff, but that's the best I can promise for now. Sorry!
